compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Ticket `47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88` built ranked similar-ticket retrieval and surfaces nothing. This story carries its results to users on every surface that creates a ticket.

Today `rebar create` warns only when a new title normalizes byte-identically to a recent one: `duplicate_create_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:117`), gated by `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (`:129`), matching on `title_norm` equality (`:103`). ADR 0122 measured that stratum at 1,431 of 1,524 recorded duplicate pairs. The remaining 93 differ in wording and are invisible to equality matching; they are why agents re-file work that already has a ticket.

## The prerequisite this story consumes

`47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88` merged as `c43d9336262d80a3371ff97cadfe15d0e92e6473` and exposes exactly one function, `rebar.similar.find_similar(tracker, *, title, description, text, exclude_id, limit)`. Three of its properties are what this story relies on, and each is already implemented rather than planned:

- It cannot fail its caller. Every failure path logs at warning level and returns `[]`; `src/rebar/similar/__init__.py` states that as its defining property.
- It accepts `exclude_id`, which keeps a ticket out of its own results.
- Its `score` is normalized to the closed interval 0 to 1, 1 most relevant, by `_score` (`src/rebar/similar/lexical.py:67-77`), which maps bm25 through `r/(1+r)`.

The field name `similar_tickets` is introduced by *this* story and is correctly absent from the tree today.

## Approach

### The advisory seam, and the five callers it actually has

The create result already carries `duplicate_warning` and `description_warning`. `_lib_writes.py` builds its return dicts by hand-copying named advisory keys — `:171-172` and `:178-179` for create, `:223-224` and `:230-231` for idea. Because every one of those sites names its keys individually, an advisory key added only to `create` is silently dropped from `idea()`'s return dict. Adding one more hand-copied key would work today and reproduce the same gap for the next advisory, so the return-dict pass-through is made generic at the `create_core` boundary.

`create_core` has five direct callers, not two, and the probe's placement decides behaviour for all of them:

| Caller | Surface | Gets the advisory |
|---|---|---|
| `composer.py:416` | `rebar create` | yes |
| `idea.py:64` | `rebar idea` | yes |
| `_lib_writes.py:145` | library `create_ticket` / `idea` | yes |
| `session_log.py:129` | `rebar session-log` | no |
| `identity.py:283` | `rebar identity` | no |

The existing `duplicate_create_warning` call sits inside `create_core` itself (`composer.py:244`), so it already runs for identity and session-log creates. Placing the ranked probe at that same point without qualification would inherit that reach, and a ranked list of similar *tickets* on an identity create is meaningless — worse, it would force an FTS5 catch-up on a write that has nothing to do with the ticket graph.

The probe is therefore skipped for `session_log`, `code_review` and `identity`. That triple is not invented here: it is rebar's existing non-work-item set, spelled identically at `_commands/_seam.py:296`, `_commands/close_precheck.py:624`, `_commands/verify_authorship.py:95`, `reducer/_api.py:24` and `_engine_support/gates.py:29`. This story reuses that classification rather than adding a sixth copy of the list. `duplicate_create_warning`'s existing reach is left as it is; narrowing it is not this story's change.

### What "generic" does and does not cover

Genericity is claimed for the **return dict** only. The two CLI stderr emitters name their keys individually by construction — `composer.py:466-467` and `idea.py:92-93` each call `_warn_stderr` per key so stdout stays pure in either output mode — and `composer.py:441` prints only `{id, alias, title}` in JSON mode. Those stay per-site and are covered by criteria of their own rather than by the genericity claim.

### Query construction and failure disposition

The advisory is computed after the write succeeds, so a retrieval failure can never fail a completed create — the disposition the existing probe already has at `recent_creates.py:151`, under the comment "an advisory notice must never fail a completed write". The query passes the just-created ticket's own id as `exclude_id`, because catch-up will already have indexed it and it would otherwise rank as its own top match.

The retrieval call site is `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py`, which imports `find_similar` at module scope; tests substitute it by monkeypatching that imported name on the `recent_creates` module, the same seam the existing probe's tests use. Every failure path yields an empty `similar_tickets` and leaves the exit status unchanged.

### Gating

The gate is `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`, the key that already gates create-time duplicate advice. This is that same advice with ranked results, so a second key would split one user-facing behaviour across two switches. No new config key is added.

`src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json` already documents the advisory contract and is extended with `similar_tickets`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar create --output json` returns a `similar_tickets` array. Checked by: a CLI test asserting the field is present.
- [x] The library `create_ticket` return dict carries `similar_tickets`. Checked by: a library test asserting the key is present.
- [x] MCP `create_ticket` output carries `similar_tickets`. Checked by: an MCP test asserting the key is present in the tool result.
- [x] The library `idea()` return dict carries `similar_tickets`. Checked by: a library test asserting the key is present on an idea create.
- [x] The `rebar idea` CLI surfaces `similar_tickets` on stderr. Checked by: a CLI test capturing stderr on an idea create.
- [x] `rebar create` surfaces `similar_tickets` on stderr in text output mode. Checked by: a CLI test capturing stderr.
- [x] Advisory keys propagate from `create_core` into the create return dict without a per-key edit. Checked by: a test adding a synthetic advisory key at the `create_core` boundary and asserting it reaches the create return dict.
- [x] The same synthetic advisory key reaches the `idea()` return dict. Checked by: the same test asserting it on an idea create.
- [x] A `session_log` create carries no `similar_tickets` advisory. Checked by: a test asserting the key is absent or empty and that no index catch-up is triggered.
- [x] An `identity` create carries no `similar_tickets` advisory. Checked by: a test asserting the key is absent or empty and that no index catch-up is triggered.
- [x] `create_result.schema.json` documents `similar_tickets`, including `score`'s range and direction. Checked by: a schema test validating a sample result against the committed schema.
- [x] A created ticket's own id never appears in its own `similar_tickets` results. Checked by: a test creating a ticket whose text matches itself strongly and asserting its id is absent.
- [x] A create exits 0 with an empty `similar_tickets` when retrieval returns empty. Checked by: a test monkeypatching `find_similar` on `recent_creates` to return `[]`.
- [x] A create exits 0 with an empty `similar_tickets` when retrieval raises. Checked by: a test monkeypatching `find_similar` on `recent_creates` to raise.
- [x] A create's ticket is written and readable when retrieval raises. Checked by: the same test reading the ticket afterwards.
- [x] `similar_tickets` is empty when `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is false. Checked by: a test with the key disabled.
- [x] No new configuration key is introduced. Checked by: `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exiting 0.
- [x] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the CI module-size gate.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
